subject: Algorithms
title: Introduction to Algorithms (CLRS)
subtitle: Comprehensive Graph, Dynamic & Tree Algorithms
author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest & Clifford Stein

pages.title: Foundations & The Role of Algorithms
bulletPoints: Definition of computational algorithm: Transforming valid input instances into well-defined output sets.
Efficiency as a bounded computational resource: Comparing insertion sort and merge sort scaling.
Correctness verification: Loop invariants (Initialization, Maintenance, and Termination proof steps).
Analyzing worst-case, average-case, and best-case execution bounds.

pages.title: Growth of Functions & Asymptotic Analysis
bulletPoints: Big-O notation (asymptotic upper bound) and Big-Omega notation (asymptotic lower bound).
Big-Theta notation (asymptotically tight bound) and small-o / small-omega strict bounds.
Standard mathematical properties: Transitivity, reflexivity, symmetry, and transpose symmetry.
Common asymptotic orders: O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n log n) < O(n^2) < O(2^n) < O(n!).

pages.title: Divide-and-Conquer Paradigm
bulletPoints: Divide, Conquer, and Combine algorithmic formulation.
Recurrence relations: Formulating execution time as T(n) = a T(n/b) + f(n).
The Substitution Method: Guessing inductive forms and establishing mathematical induction.
The Recursion-Tree Method: Visualizing per-level computational cost and total tree depth.

pages.title: The Master Theorem & Analysis
bulletPoints: The Master Method: Solving recurrences of the form T(n) = a T(n/b) + f(n).
Case 1: f(n) = O(n^(log_b a - epsilon)) -> T(n) = Theta(n^(log_b a)).
Case 2: f(n) = Theta(n^(log_b a) log^k n) -> T(n) = Theta(n^(log_b a) log^(k+1) n).
Case 3: f(n) = Omega(n^(log_b a + epsilon)) with regularity condition -> T(n) = Theta(f(n)).

pages.title: Heapsort & Priority Queues
bulletPoints: Binary Heap data structure: Array-based representation with left child (2i) and right child (2i+1).
The Max-Heap property: Parent key greater than or equal to children keys.
Max-Heapify procedure: O(log n) sinking operation restoring heap invariant.
Build-Max-Heap: Linear-time O(n) construction through bottom-up heapification.

pages.title: Priority Queue Operations
bulletPoints: Extract-Max: Removing top element and re-heapifying in O(log n).
Heap-Increase-Key: Bubbling modified keys up to the root in O(log n).
Heap-Insert: Appending element and maintaining max-heap structural invariants.
Applications: CPU job scheduling, Dijkstra's shortest path, and Huffman coding trees.

pages.title: Quicksort & Partitioning
bulletPoints: Divide-and-conquer strategy: In-place array sorting without auxiliary memory allocations.
Lomuto and Hoare partitioning schemes: Invariant maintenance and pivot element placement.
Worst-case O(n^2) behavior on already sorted arrays and deep recursion stack depths.
Average-case O(n log n) analysis: Proving expected linearithmic time across random permutations.

pages.title: Randomized Quicksort & Analysis
bulletPoints: Randomized pivot selection: Preventing adversarial input degradations.
Indicator random variables in algorithm analysis.
Expected running time proof: Summing pairwise comparison probabilities across sorted ranks.
Stack depth optimization: Tail-recursion elimination bounding auxiliary stack space to O(log n).

pages.title: Sorting in Linear Time
bulletPoints: Lower bounds for comparison sorting: Decision-tree model proving Omega(n log n) comparisons.
Counting Sort: Stable integer sorting in O(n + k) using prefix-sum frequency arrays.
Radix Sort: Multi-pass digit-by-digit stable sorting running in O(d(n + k)) time.
Bucket Sort: Distributing elements across uniform intervals for expected O(n) performance.

pages.title: Medians and Order Statistics
bulletPoints: The Selection Problem: Finding the i-th smallest element in an unordered set of n keys.
Randomized-Select: Expected linear time O(n) algorithm based on quicksort partitioning.
Worst-case linear time: The Median-of-Medians (BFPRT) algorithm partitioning into groups of 5.
Recurrence analysis of Median-of-Medians: T(n) <= T(ceil(n/5)) + T(7n/10 + 6) + O(n) -> O(n).

pages.title: Elementary Data Structures & Hash Tables
bulletPoints: Stacks, queues, linked lists (singly, doubly, and circular variants).
Direct-address tables vs Hash tables: Resolving large key-space mappings.
Collision resolution: Chaining with linked lists vs Open Addressing (linear, quadratic, double hashing).
Hash functions: Division method, multiplication method, and Universal Hashing guarantees.

pages.title: Binary Search Trees (BST)
bulletPoints: The BST property: Key(left child) <= Key(parent) <= Key(right child).
In-order, pre-order, and post-order tree traversals in O(n) time.
Search, Minimum, Maximum, Successor, and Predecessor operations in O(h) time.
Insertion and node deletion with structural re-linking (handling 0, 1, or 2 children cases).

pages.title: Red-Black Trees: Balanced Search
bulletPoints: Red-Black structural properties: Color rule, root rule, leaf rule, red rule, and black-height rule.
Bounding tree height: A Red-Black tree with n internal nodes has height h <= 2 log(n + 1).
Tree rotations: Left-Rotate and Right-Rotate maintaining the binary search tree property.
Insertion rebalancing: Handling three color/rotation cases to restore black-height invariants.

pages.title: Red-Black Tree Deletion & Augmentation
bulletPoints: Node removal in Red-Black trees: Tracking displaced node colors and introducing double-black tokens.
Four deletion fixup cases: Sibling colors, nephew colors, and rotation sequences.
Augmenting data structures: Storing sub-tree sizes to create dynamic Order-Statistic Trees.
Interval Trees: Storing intervals [low, high] and querying overlapping segments in O(log n) time.

pages.title: Dynamic Programming Paradigm
bulletPoints: Two core ingredients: Optimal Substructure and Overlapping Subproblems.
Top-down memoization vs Bottom-up iterative table construction.
Reconstructing optimal solutions: Backtracking through decision matrix pointers.
Rod Cutting Problem: Formulating recurrence r_n = max_{1<=i<=n}(p_i + r_{n-i}).

pages.title: Classic Dynamic Programming Algorithms
bulletPoints: Matrix-Chain Multiplication: Minimizing scalar multiplications via optimal parenthesization.
Longest Common Subsequence (LCS): Substring matching in O(m n) time and space.
0/1 Knapsack Problem: Dynamic programming table construction over capacity constraints.
Optimal Binary Search Trees: Minimizing expected search cost given key access probabilities.

pages.title: Greedy Algorithms & Matroids
bulletPoints: Greedy-choice property: A globally optimal solution can be arrived at by making locally optimal choices.
Activity Selection Problem: Proving the earliest finish-time greedy choice is optimal.
Huffman Codes: Optimal prefix-free character encodings constructed via greedy min-heaps.
Theoretical foundations: Matroid theory, independent sets, and the greedy guarantee.

pages.title: Amortized Analysis Techniques
bulletPoints: Aggregate analysis: Computing average cost per operation over a sequence of n operations.
The Accounting Method: Assigning artificial charges (credits) to lightweight operations to pay for expensive ones.
The Potential Method: Defining state energy Phi(D) such that amortized cost c_i' = c_i + Phi(D_i) - Phi(D_{i-1}).
Case studies: Dynamic array resizing (doubling strategy) and binary counter increment sequences.

pages.title: B-Trees & Multiway Search
bulletPoints: Disk-based storage considerations: Minimizing disk block I/O operations through multi-way branching.
B-Tree properties: Minimum degree t, node capacity [t-1, 2t-1], and uniform leaf depth.
Search and insertion: Proactive root splitting during downward traversal.
B-Tree node deletion: Merging underflowing sibling nodes and borrowing keys.

pages.title: Fibonacci Heaps & Mergeable Heaps
bulletPoints: Structure of Fibonacci Heaps: Collections of min-heap-ordered trees with lazy structural consolidation.
Asymptotic bounds: O(1) amortized insertion, find-minimum, decrease-key, and union operations.
Bounding maximum degree: Proving tree sizes grow exponentially with golden ratio phi.
Cascading cuts: Maintaining structural balance during repeated decrease-key invocations.

pages.title: Graph Representations & Traversals
bulletPoints: Adjacency matrix vs Adjacency list: Space complexity and edge lookup trade-offs.
Breadth-First Search (BFS): Queue-based level exploration, discovery tree, and shortest path in unweighted graphs.
Depth-First Search (DFS): Stack/recursion traversal, discovery and finish timestamping.
Parenthesis theorem, classification of edges (Tree, Back, Forward, Cross), and Topological Sorting.

pages.title: Strongly Connected Components & Decomposition
bulletPoints: Directed graph connectivity: Mutual reachability between vertex pairs.
Kosaraju-Sharir Algorithm: Utilizing two DFS passes on graph G and transpose G^T in O(V + E).
Tarjan's strongly connected components algorithm: Single DFS pass tracking lowlink values.
Component DAG condensation: Transforming cyclic networks into topological dependency graphs.

pages.title: Minimum Spanning Trees (MST)
bulletPoints: The MST problem: Connecting all vertices with minimum total edge weight without introducing cycles.
The Cut Property: A light edge crossing a cut that respects an MST subset belongs to the MST.
Kruskal's Algorithm: Greedy edge sorting and Disjoint-Set (Union-Find) cycle detection in O(E log E).
Prim's Algorithm: Growing a single tree using priority queues in O(E + V log V) with Fibonacci heaps.

pages.title: Single-Source Shortest Paths: Dijkstra
bulletPoints: Relaxation technique: Maintaining d[v] upper bounds and updating d[v] = min(d[v], d[u] + w(u,v)).
Dijkstra's Algorithm: Greedy shortest path discovery for non-negative edge weights.
Correctness proof: Inductive verification that extracted vertices have reached exact shortest paths.
Implementation complexity: O(V^2) with array, O(E log V) with binary heap, O(E + V log V) with Fibonacci heap.

pages.title: Shortest Paths: Bellman-Ford & DAGs
bulletPoints: Bellman-Ford Algorithm: Handling arbitrary edge weights and detecting negative-weight cycles.
Execution mechanics: Relaxing all |V|-1 edges iteratively across |V| rounds in O(V E) time.
Shortest paths in Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs): Single topological pass solving shortest paths in O(V + E).
Critical Path Method (CPM): Finding longest paths in DAGs for project scheduling.

pages.title: All-Pairs Shortest Paths
bulletPoints: Matrix multiplication formulation: Extending paths via dynamic programming in O(V^3 log V).
Floyd-Warshall Algorithm: Dynamic programming over intermediate vertices k running in Theta(V^3).
Transitive Closure of directed graphs using Warshall's boolean matrix formulation.
Johnson's Algorithm: Reweighting graphs via Bellman-Ford and running Dijkstra from each vertex in O(V E log V).

pages.title: Maximum Flow & Network Optimization
bulletPoints: Flow networks: Source s, sink t, capacity constraints c(u,v), and flow conservation laws.
Residual networks, augmenting paths, and residual capacity definitions.
Ford-Fulkerson Method: Iteratively augmenting flow along residual paths.
Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem: Maximum flow through a network equals the minimum capacity across all s-t cuts.

pages.title: Edmonds-Karp & Push-Relabel Algorithms
bulletPoints: Edmonds-Karp Algorithm: Implementing Ford-Fulkerson using BFS for augmenting paths in O(V E^2).
Maximum Bipartite Matching: Transforming matching problems into unit-capacity max-flow instances.
Push-Relabel (Preflow-Push) framework: Replacing global augmenting paths with local vertex operations.
Height functions, overflowing vertices, discharge operations, and O(V^3) relabel-to-front complexity.

pages.title: NP-Completeness & Tractability
bulletPoints: Complexity classes: P (polynomial-time solvable) and NP (polynomial-time verifiable).
Polynomial-time reductions: Transforming problem A to problem B in polynomial time (A <=_p B).
Cook-Levin Theorem: Proving Satisfiability (SAT) is NP-Complete via non-deterministic Turing machine encoding.
Classic NP-Complete problems: 3-SAT, Clique, Vertex Cover, Hamiltonian Cycle, and Traveling Salesperson (TSP).

pages.title: Approximation Algorithms & Randomized Methods
bulletPoints: Approximation ratio: Bounding the sub-optimality factor rho(n) = max(C/C*, C*/C).
Vertex Cover 2-approximation: Maximal matching greedy strategy.
Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP): Triangle inequality 2-approximation using MST preorder traversal.
Christofides 1.5-approximation algorithm using Minimum Weight Perfect Matching on odd-degree vertices.
